verdict.rationale: Temporal documents first-party SDKs on its own docs site: an SDK architecture page describes Workflow and Activity execution APIs, and there are per-language developer guides for Python and TypeScript, including a Python walkthrough, TypeScript versioning docs, and AI integrations. A community user also reports quick vendor fixes to the library. missing for 10: an explicit enumeration of all supported SDK languages, and deeper independent hands-on corroboration of SDK quality across languages.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: They feature APIs for Workflow and Activity execution, automatic retries, and resilience mechanisms, making it easier to build fault-tolerant applications.
There's also a short walkthrough of how to use the Temporal primitives (Activities, Workflows, and Workers) to build and run a Temporal application to get you up and running.
During an evaluation I found a bug in their library. I went to their Slack, posted about it, and they gave a workaround in 15 minutes, created an issue in 30, and had a bugfix PR ready the next day.
